chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Tayalisi, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, has always been our Lord; and Knowledge is His very Essence with no object of knowledge, and Hearing is His very Essence with no object of hearing, and Sight is His very Essence with no object of sight, and Power is His very Essence with no object of power.

Then, when He created things and there came to be an object of knowledge, the Knowledge from Him was applied to the known, and Hearing to the heard, and Sight to the seen, and Power to the empowered.'
He (Abu Baseer) said: 'I said, "Has God always been moving?" He (the Imam) said: "God is Exalted above that. Movement is a quality originated through action."
I said, "Has God always been speaking?" He said: "Speech is an originated quality, it is not eternal. God, Mighty and Majestic, was — and He did not speak."'

key_terms.الذات: The divine Self/Essence — the fundamental nature of God, the ground of all attributes
key_terms.صفة محدثة: Originated/created attribute — one that came into being in time, as opposed to an eternal essential attribute
key_terms.عز وجل: Mighty and Majestic — standard honorific for God (azzu wa jalla)
key_terms.لم يزل: Has always been / never ceased — formula denoting eternity and unchangingness of God

ai.seo_question: Are God's attributes identical with His essence in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses one of the most profound questions in Islamic theology: the nature of God's essential attributes before creation. The Imam teaches the doctrine of 'Sifat al-Dhat' (Attributes of the Self), affirming that God's Knowledge, Hearing, Sight, and Power are identical with His Essence — not separate from it — even when there was no created object to which they related. This was a direct response to theological debates in early Islam about whether God's attributes were His essence or additions to it. Furthermore, by declaring that movement and speech are 'originated' attributes belonging to the realm of action (not essence), the Imam refutes both anthropomorphism (tashbih) and the Mu'tazilite claim of eternal divine speech, safeguarding the absolute transcendence and simplicity of the divine Being.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Khalid Al Tayalisy, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic never ceased to be our Lord<sup>azwj</sup>; and the Knowledge is His<sup>azwj</sup> Self and (even though) there may be nothing to be known, and the Hearing is His<sup>azwj</sup> Self and (even though) there may be nothing to be heard, and the Seeing is His<sup>azwj</sup> Self and (even though) there may be nothing to be seen, and the Power is His<sup>azwj</sup> Self and (even though) there may be nothing to be empowered upon.

So when He<sup>azwj</sup> Created the things, and it was the known (things), the Knowledge Occurred from Him<sup>azwj</sup> upon the known, and the Hearing upon the heard, and the Seeing upon the seen, and the Power upon the empowered’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> does not cease to be moving’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is more Exalted from that. The movement is a quality created by the deed’.

I said, ‘So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> did not cease to be Speaking’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The speech is a created quality, it is not with the eternality. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic was, and He<sup>azwj</sup> did not Speak’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Tayalisi from Safwan ibn Yahya from ibn Maskan from abu Basir who has said the following.

“I heard abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) saying, ‘The Exalted, the Glorious, Allah, our Lord, is Eternal. Knowledge is His self even if there is nothing to be known. Hearing is His self even if there is nothing to be heard. Seeing is His-self even when there is nothing to be seen. Power is His self even if there is nothing to feel the power.

When He brought things into existence the perceptible objects became the objects of His knowledge, His hearing applied to audible objects, His seeing to visible objects and His power to the objects that feel power.’”
Abu Basir adds; “I further asked, ‘Has Allah always been in motion?” He replied, “Allah is High Exalted above that. Motion is an attribute that is created through action.”

I asked, “Did Allah always have the ability to speak?” He replied, “ Speech is a created attribute and not an eternal one. Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, existed when there was nothing able to speak.”
